chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran Al-Halbi, from Ayoub ibn Atiyya Al-Hazza', who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) distributed the Fay (booty/wealth), and Ali (peace be upon him) was assigned a piece of land. He dug a well in it, and water gushed out towards the sky in the form of a camel's neck. So he named it 'Yanbu' (the gusher).

The herald of good news came with the good news, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Give the good news to the inheritors. It is a charity, irrevocable, for the pilgrims of the House of Allah and the passers-by in the Way of Allah. It shall not be sold, nor gifted, nor inherited.'
So whoever sells it or gifts it, upon him is the Curse of Allah, the Angels, and all people. Allah will not accept from him any exchange or ransom.

key_terms.لَا تُبَاعُ وَ لَا تُوهَبُ وَ لَا تُورَث: Not sold, not gifted, and not inherited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling or gifting the Prophet's charity land according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the unique status of Imam Ali’s (as) land grant as an irrevocable charity (*sadaqah khalidah*) for the benefit of pilgrims and travelers, emphasizing its perpetual nature distinct from ordinary property. The Prophet’s declaration that it 'cannot be sold, gifted, or inherited' establishes a legal precedent for *waqf* in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the asset remains dedicated to public utility. The severe curse upon those who alter its status underscores the sanctity of preserving charitable endowments for the sake of Allah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Yahya Bin Imran Al Halby, from Ayoub Bin Atiyya Al Haza’a who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> distributed Al-Fey, so Ali<sup>asws</sup> got a land and there were springs in it. So the water came out gushing towards the sky as if it was a neck of the camel. Thus it was named as Yanba (gusher).

So the herald of good news came with the good news, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Give the good news to the inheritors. It is a charity, irrevocable, in the Pilgrims of the House of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the passers-by in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. It can neither be sold, not gifted, nor inherited.

So the one who sells it, or gifts it, so upon him is the Curse of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Angels, and the people altogether. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will not Accept from him an exchange nor a ransom’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya ibn ‘Imran al-Halabiy from Ayyub ibn ‘Atiyyah al-Hadhdha’ who has narrated the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, distributed the assets captured from the enemy among the Muslims.
The share of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was a piece of land. He dug a well and water gushed toward the sky like the neck of a camel. He called it Yanbu‘a.

A bearer of good news came to him with good news and Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, “You must give the good news to the heirs. It is an irrevocable charity and complete for those who perform al-Hajj of the house of Allah and the by-passers. It will not be sold, gifted or inherited.
Those who buy or gift it, will be subjected to the condemnation of Allah, the angels and all people; and Allah will not divert it from him or accept ransom.’””
